subject: Brazilian winger Sergio Barboza becomes first outfield player to play in all six confederations
title: Six confederations, one full passport

lines.vo: Six confederations. One winger. One very full passport.
lines.footage: Barboza Tahiti highlight clip, stadium wide shot

lines.vo: Sergio Barboza: Laos, Nepal, Malta, Angola. His CV is a travel diary.
lines.footage: kit and match clips from Laos, Nepal, Malta, Angola (no club logos on screen)

lines.vo: ESPN says he is the first outfield player to do it in FIFA-affiliated leagues.
In September he reached Tahiti with no club. About three hundred fans paid six dollars a month to back him.
lines.footage: Tahiti arrival b-roll, fans in a stand, phone screens

lines.vo: They voted on his decisions in a WhatsApp group. Three hundred assistant managers.
Debut: two goals, an assist, a five-one win. In five games: four goals, four assists.
lines.footage: Tahiti debut match highlight, stat graphic over match clips

lines.vo: Unpaid, bar the room. A cyclone then doubled his flight home: nearly three thousand dollars.
Next stop: Africa. Cyclones, you have been warned.
lines.footage: map graphic, Barboza smiling, boarding b-roll

facts_used: Barboza, 33, has played for clubs in all six confederations, including Laos, Cambodia, Nepal, Angola, Malta and Tahiti (news 157, espn.com)
ESPN says he is the first outfield player to do so in FIFA-affiliated leagues (news 157, espn.com)
He reached Tahiti on 21 September with no club; about 300 followers paid 6 dollars a month and voted on decisions in a WhatsApp group (news 157)
He scored twice and set up another in a 5-1 win on his Tahiti debut; four goals and four assists in five games; unpaid apart from accommodation (news 157)
A cyclone doubled his return flight to about 3,000 dollars; he plans to go back to Africa to score and assist there (news 157)
